Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
248 AM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* A potent winter storm continues to impact the region through 
  Friday morning, bringing heavy Sierra snow, strong winds, and 
  hazardous travel.

* Strong winds will continue over Sierra ridges, with gusty winds
  across western Nevada valleys and northeast California.

* A brief break in precipitation Friday afternoon through Saturday
  morning will be followed by another system arriving Saturday
  afternoon, with yet another system on Thanksgiving week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A potent, early season winter storm will continue to deliver heavy 
snow to the Sierra through the evening, compounding already 
treacherous mountain travel conditions throughout the day. 
Meanwhile, light snow will become more steady across the Greater 
Reno-Carson-Minden area between 5 AM and 10 AM PST this morning, 
greeting the morning commute with slick, snow-covered roads and 
reduced visibilities. 

The colder, more unstable side of the storm moves into the region by 
the afternoon, making quick bursts of heavier snow (and rain in 
lowest W NV valleys) more common during the afternoon and evening 
hours. Coverage of snow showers will be greatest across the Sierra, 
courtesy of orographic lift, but a few snow showers should reach W 
Nevada as a surface cold front sweeps through. Moreover, colder post-
frontal winds overspreading warmer lake waters may support lake 
enhanced snowband E/SE of Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake -- the latter 
is more likely given a more favorable wind direction/longer fetch. 
Whichever the source, late afternoon snow showers may renew travel 
impacts during the evening commute. 

Showers taper off as the evening progresses, but a shortwave trough 
passage reinvigorates shower activity Friday morning. Before the 
storm finally departs Friday afternoon, it will have brought an 
additional 15 to 30 inches of snow to the Sierra crest and 4-12 
inches broadly above 5500 ft. Meanwhile, valley floors may receive
up to 3 inches of new snow. 

Weak high pressure in between storms will provide a brief period of 
dry, albeit very cold, weather Friday afternoon through Saturday 
morning. This would allow an opportunity for trans-Sierra travel if 
road conditions improve enough (check with CalTrans and NDOT for 
latest road conditions) before our next storm arrives Saturday 
afternoon. However, a few sneaky weather concerns arise during this 
timeframe, all of which would be realized Friday night into Saturday 
morning. First is the potential for icy roads as daytime snowmelt 
refreezes overnight Friday. Second are areas of freezing fog 
across NE CA and Sierra valleys. And finally, the prospect for 
bitterly cold nighttime lows as temperatures fall into the single 
digits to teens. Some notoriously colder locales (e.g., Bodie, 
Bridgeport, Truckee, etc.) may even flirt sub-zero temperatures 
early Saturday morning. 

As mentioned, the next storm arrives saturday afternoon and delivers 
periods of increased breezes and showers through Sunday. This storm 
will be much weaker than its predecessor, with 3-6" of snow along 
the Sierra crest and up to 3" above 6000 ft. Lingering cold air will 
keep snow levels at or below valley floors, but spillover into W 
Nevada is much less certain. Nevertheless, a trace to 1" is on the 
table for the Greater Reno area and other W NV communities by 
Monday. The weather pattern remains unsettled leading up to 
Thanksgiving with additional storms posing impacts to holiday travel 
and festivities. Be sure to keep up with the latest forecast if 
planning to travel for Thanksgiving. 

-Salas

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: Periods of -SN and low clouds will continue to lower 
CIGS/VIS to IFR conditions through the afternoon, especially between 
13Z and 19Z when snow will be heaviest. Snow becomes showery in the 
afternoon, leading to more intermittent periods of -SHSN and IFR 
conditions through Friday morning. An additional 1-2" of runway 
accumulation will be possible by Friday morning, with a 20-30% 
chance of seeing more than 2 inches. Otherwise, breezy W/NW (gusts 
up 20 kts) and LLWS concerns will accompany a cold frontal passage 
this afternoon. 

Regional Outlook: Periods of heavy snow and IFR/LIFR conditions 
persist through Friday morning at KTRK-KTVL-KMMH, with an additional 
6-12" of runway accumulation possible. Gusts of 25-30 kts will also 
be possible at Sierra terminals, with LLWS and mountain wave 
turbulence concerns continuing. Light snowfall and IFR conditions 
are expected at KCXP-KMEV, with 1-3" of runway accumulation through 
Friday morning.  

24-72 Hour Outlook: Heavy mountain snow and valley rain/snow showers 
taper off by Friday morning. FZFG may impact KTRK and KTVL Friday 
night into Saturday morning. Another storm arrives Saturday 
afternoon, bringing periods of snow through Sunday.  

-Salas

&&

.AVALANCHE...

An early season winter storm system will bring heavy snow to all 
avalanche center terrain through Friday AM. 

* Snowfall Totals and Rates: Expect an additional 15-30 inches of
  snow above 7000 feet through Friday morning, with 4-12 inches 
  possible at lake level in Tahoe and along US-395 in Mono County.
  Heaviest snowfall rates will occur this morning and afternoon 
  at 2-3 inches per hour. 

* SWE, SLRs, and Snow Levels: Along the crest, additional SWE of 1.5-
  2.5 inches with up to 1.5 inches elsewhere. SLRs will be 
  relatively high at 11-13:1, and locally up to 14:1. Snow levels 
  remain below 6000 feet for the duration of the storm. 

* Ridgetop Wind Gusts and Thunder: Southwest winds gusting over 100 
  mph this morning, becoming W/NW gusts up to 50 mph in the 
  afternoon. 15-20% chance for thunder along the Sierra Crest this 
  afternoon. Convective snow bands could produce locally higher 
  snowfall rates up to 4 inches per hour. HRICH/Jyler
